findings.finding: Audioboom, the closest listed pure-play peer, reported a record Q3 2026 on 14 Oct with adjusted EBITDA ahead of market expectations and a raised FY EBITDA floor, citing the first meaningful wave of US midterm political ad spend — but its Q3 revenue growth slowed to 17% from ~30% in H1, so the read on Acast's top line is mixed-positive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Acast rose ~20% at the open on the Q3 2025 revenue surprise (EFN, https://efn.se/forvaltaren-jublar-over-acast-rapport-superstark) but gapped to 41 and closed -1.6% on the Q2 2026 record-revenue print (MFN price box on the Q2 release).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Acast's tape did not react (32.35 on 14 Oct, flat at ~32 since), so either the read-through is ignored or discounted by the peer's revenue deceleration; if priced as a positive the stock would have firmed off its 60-day -13% drawdown into the print.
findings.independence: Spotify Q3 2026 podcast sponsorship growth, different source: https://ppc.land/spotifys-direct-ad-sales-drop-eur53m-as-biddable-channels-drive-9-growth/

findings.finding: Spotify's Q3 2026 ad-supported revenue grew 10% reported (9% cc) from 3% in each of the first two quarters, with management naming podcast sponsorships as a growth driver — the largest podcast-ad seller's demand signal for the same quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed Acast reaction to Spotify prints; Acast's own revenue surprises have moved it from -1.6% (Q2 2026) to ~+20% (Q3 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Spotify is a competitor as well as a market gauge and its direct-sales channel shrank (-EUR53m), so the read is ambiguous; Acast closed 32.65 -> 32.40 -> 32.00 across that report, i.e. no positive repricing.

findings.finding: Reported Q3 net sales get two non-organic tailwinds that Q2 did not have: USD/SEK averaged 9.65 in Q3 2026 vs 9.51 in Q3 2025 (Q2 was a headwind, 9.37 vs 9.66; GBP/SEK 12.97 vs 12.82) and Backyard Ventures (~$16m 2025 revenue) consolidated from ~11 Aug, together worth roughly 4-5 points of reported growth on top of organic; against a ~SEK 798m (+24%) estimate that implies only ~20% organic, reported revenue is more likely above than below.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 reported-vs-organic gap (28% vs 29%) passed without comment; the market has traded organic growth and margins, not FX.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference only: FX is visible to every analyst and the acquisition was announced; the bar it beats is a single snippet-only estimate, so this is capped small. If priced, the estimate would already sit near SEK 820-830m.

findings.finding: Q3 laps the company's strongest quarter (Q3 2025 organic +41%, North America +58%) while listens grew only 2% y/y in Q2, so a visible organic deceleration from 29% is likely and growth rests on ARPLV.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock has de-rated ~20% from its June high (EUR 3.72 on 5 June per boerse.de) through a period with no negative company news, consistent with deceleration already being discounted.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the comp is public and the 60-day run-up is -12.9%; a market that had not priced it would still be near the 37-38 SEK July level.
findings.independence: Audioboom's revenue deceleration to 17% in Q3 from ~30% in H1 points the same way: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/audioboom-group--boom/q3-trading-update/9821291
